did_you_know: Standby mode (phantom load) can account for up to 10% of your total electricity bill.
Air conditioners are typically the #1 energy consumer in a home, contributing 25–40% of electricity bills.
Switching from incandescent to LED bulbs can cut lighting energy use by up to 85%.
A full refrigerator is more energy-efficient than a half-empty one — it retains cold better.
Washing clothes in cold water uses 90% less energy than washing in hot water.
Unplugging your phone charger when not in use can save up to 5 kWh per year per charger.
Using a microwave instead of an electric oven for small meals saves about 80% energy.
Solar water heaters can reduce water heating costs by 50–80%.
Ceiling fans use 98% less energy than air conditioners.
A dripping faucet can waste 3,000+ gallons of water per year, indirectly wasting pump energy.

myths_vs_facts.myth: Turning lights on and off wastes more electricity than leaving them on.
myths_vs_facts.fact: This is FALSE for modern LED and CFL bulbs. Switching them off saves energy every single time.
FALSE. Screensavers don't reduce power consumption. Setting the monitor to sleep mode does.

myths_vs_facts.myth: Charging your phone overnight damages the battery and wastes electricity.
myths_vs_facts.fact: PARTIALLY TRUE. Modern phones stop charging at 100%, but keeping them at 100% long-term degrades battery health.

myths_vs_facts.myth: Ceiling fans cool the room temperature.
myths_vs_facts.fact: FALSE. Fans cool people, not rooms, by creating a wind-chill effect. Turn them off when you leave.

myths_vs_facts.myth: New appliances don't need energy-saving habits.
myths_vs_facts.fact: FALSE. Even energy-efficient appliances waste power if used carelessly (e.g., leaving fridge door open).
